title: JAX bug
description: A bug in JAX found with the Lean model. The file name is the identifier of the bug. The fields from title to fix, and jax_version, are the sections of an upstream issue, in this order.

title.description: One line that names the bug.

status.description: found: the reproducer shows the bug. proven: the reproducer shows the bug, and a Lean theorem refutes our model of the rule. reported: an upstream issue exists. fixed: a JAX release contains a fix.

priority.description: A conservative judgment, reviewed before filing. P0: aborts the process, or a silent wrong result on ordinary inputs. P1: a silent wrong result on edge inputs that real code reaches, such as empty arrays, infinities or a jnp function. P2: an exception where a result is expected, or a silent wrong result only on inputs that jnp does not emit. P3: an inconsistency where the behaviour is arguably correct.

primitive.description: The lax primitive, as named in lax, or the public function outside lax, such as `jax.scipy.special.logsumexp`, if the bug is in its Python code and not in a rule of a primitive.

source.description: The faulty code, as jax/_src/<file>.py:<line> of jax_version.

lean_refutation.description: The fully qualified name of the Lean theorem that refutes our model of the rule, if the model covers it.

upstream_issue.description: The URL of the upstream issue.

duplicate_search.description: The search for an existing upstream issue, repeated before filing. null only if upstream_issue is set and no search was needed to find it.

queries.description: The searches tried, each as `<owner>/<repository>: <query>`, over issues and pull requests.

found.description: The issues and pull requests found that concern the same code, in Markdown, one per array entry: its URL and how it relates to this bug. Empty if none was found.

maybe_intended.description: Why a maintainer could call the behaviour intended, in Markdown, one line per array entry, or null if nothing speaks for it. A bug whose expected behaviour rests on our reading and not on a written promise says so here.

description.description: What goes wrong, as a user of JAX sees it, in Markdown, one line per array entry: the input that triggers the bug, what JAX does, and which cases are affected. The title, description, expected, reproducer, cause and fix stand alone, as in an upstream issue: they do not mention Lean, the model or files of this repository. scripts/bugs.py checks this.

expected.description: What JAX should do instead, and on what authority: the docstring, the StableHLO spec, the mathematics, or another path of JAX that gets it right. In Markdown, one line per array entry.

reproducer.description: A Python script that runs on its own, one line per array entry. It prints what JAX computes, and a comment below each print states the output: `# output: <text>` where JAX is correct, and `# desired: <text>` followed by `# actual: <text>` where it is not. scripts/bugs.py checks that the script prints these outputs.

cause.description: Why it goes wrong, in the source of JAX or XLA, in Markdown, one line per array entry.

fix.description: How to fix it, in Markdown, one line per array entry, or null if no fix is proposed.

lean.description: How the Lean model covers the bug, or why it does not, in Markdown, one line per array entry. The only text that may refer to Lean or to this repository.

related.description: The identifiers of related bugs, which the dashboard links to.

jax_version.description: The JAX version on which the bug was found.

fixed_in.description: The first JAX version that contains a fix.
